newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal presents privatisation plan to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Portugal presents privatisation plan to 2000.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government on Wednesday presented a plan for privatisations over the final two years of the decade that would earn at least 800 billion escudos.

Sales in 1998-99 would include stakes in national airline TAP and the state airport and port authorities, as well as further chunks of state-controlled oil company Petrogal, electricity concern EDP and cement concern Cimpor, the Finance Ministry announced.
"It is reasonable to estimate average annual earnings of 400 billion escudos," the ministry said.
The government, which has been disposing of state assets at a fast pace since taking office in October 1995, expects to earn some 500 billion escudos from privatisations in 1997.

The one sector in which there would be no further sales was the financial sector, with the government retaining its 100 percent stake in savings bank Caixa Geral de Depositos and its Banco Nacional Ultramarino subsidiary.

As with the 1996-97 programme, which included Portugal Telecom, the privatisations were aimed at boosting competitiveness within the economy, improving the financial position and efficiency of the companies concerned and lowering the level of state debt.

Within the industrial sector, the government said that it would be selling more of the 35 percent holding it still has in Cimpor. It did not say how much would be sold but said it intended to retain a holding to "guarantee shareholder stability."
Stakes in national carrier TAP would also be sold to a strategic partner or partners with a view to boosting the loss-making company's ability to compete.
The state would also retain a golden share in Petrogal at the end of the privatisation process.

The government currently holds 55 percent with 45 percent in the hands of a private consortium made up of leading Portuguese firms and banks. Negotiations are under way for Aramco, the Saudi Arabian oil company, to take a stake in the company.
